ai.title: Remove getInitialPrompt from backend/src/prompts.ts
ai.summary: Deleted getInitialPrompt function from backend/src/prompts.ts, removing ~95 lines of inline prompt instructions and examples. Updated musings.knowledge.md to mark 'prompt engineer for knowledge changes' and 'context loading' problems as resolved, and added a new issue for indentation failures during multi-level edits. Scope limited to backend prompt logic and internal knowledge base.

eli5.text: The team removed a large block of step-by-step instructions that the assistant previously followed when starting a coding task, leaving only streamlined backend prompt logic. If you maintain or review the internal documentation, you'll now see two previously open problems marked as resolved, plus a newly recorded issue where the assistant sometimes messes up indentation when making several edits at once. This is purely behind-the-scenes housekeeping with no visible effect on your interactions today.

ai.title: Refine diff generation prompt and system instructions
ai.summary: Updated `backend/src/prompts.ts` to include explicit `<old>`/`<new>` block examples and simplified indentation analysis instructions. Modified `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` to clarify that file edits are applied automatically without user intervention. Changes affect internal prompt logic for diff generation and system context.

eli5.text: The assistant now gets clearer, step-by-step examples showing exactly how to mark up the old and new versions of a file when it wants to make a change, instead of describing the format in words. This is internal housekeeping that makes the tool generating edits more precise behind the scenes. If you looked at the system guiding the assistant, you'd see a concrete before-and-after example and tidier wording about edits being applied automatically. The change is live today and only affects how the assistant prepares file modifications, not what you see in the app.

ai.title: Await websocket callbacks in onWebsocketAction
ai.summary: onWebsocketAction now awaits callbacks via Promise.all instead of firing them without await. This ensures errors thrown by callbacks are caught and logged synchronously. Scope limited to backend/src/websockets/websocket-action.ts. Error logging now includes the full msg object alongside the message.

eli5.text: When a message comes in through the real-time connection between your browser and the app's server, the part of the system that runs in response now waits for all those responses to finish before moving on. If any of them run into a problem, the system will catch that problem and write it down along with the full original message, making it easier to figure out what went wrong later. This is a behind-the-scenes tweak that improves reliability and debugging without changing what you see on the screen.

ai.title: Remove unused addUserMessage logic
ai.summary: Deleted `addUserMessage` from `src/index.ts` and removed the unused `promptClaude` import in `backend/src/prompts.ts`. Direct `chatStorage.addMessage` calls replace the helper in `handleUserInput`. Scope limited to internal cleanup; no user-facing behavior change.

eli5.text: The program had some leftover building blocks that were no longer being used, so it removed them. If you looked at the chat history, you wouldn't see any difference because the way messages are saved was already handled by other parts of the code. This is a behind-the-scenes cleanup that doesn't change what you experience.

ai.title: Fix chat storage bug
ai.summary: ChatStorage.addMessage signature changed from (chatId, message) to (chat, message) in src/chat-storage.ts. Callers in src/index.ts updated to pass currentChat object directly instead of currentChat.id. This ensures the in-memory chat object reference is mutated and saved correctly.

eli5.text: Starting today, the assistant now correctly saves each message to the right spot in your chat history. Previously, a bookkeeping detail caused some of your messages to land in the wrong chat thread, so conversations could get jumbled or appear out of order when you came back to them. Now every incoming message sticks to the current chat you have open, so your history stays intact and matches what you sent and received.

ai.title: Fix createFileBlock arg order in prompts.ts
ai.summary: Corrected argument order for `createFileBlock` in `backend/src/prompts.ts` by moving `filePath` to the first position in three example generation calls. Added debug logging for message counts and empty diff block warnings to aid troubleshooting. Internal fix affecting prompt generation logic only.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the system that asks the AI assistant to write code now passes file information in the correct order when building example responses, so those instructional examples no longer break during generation. You wouldn't notice this directly, but it prevents subtle errors in how the assistant learns to format its replies. The team also added logging so they can better track how many conversation turns are being processed and spot cases where no code changes come back, making future troubleshooting easier.

ai.title: Multi-message continuation handling in promptClaudeAndGetFileChanges
ai.summary: Refactored `continuedMessage` to `continuedMessages` array in `backend/src/prompts.ts` to support multi-turn continuation. Added explicit user prompt 'Please continue from the very next character' when generation pauses without stop marker or tool call. Removed premature `isComplete` flag setting on tool chunk receipt to ensure proper state transition. Also removed debug `console.log` for `currentChat` in `src/index.ts`.

eli5.text: The assistant can now keep a running conversation going in multi-step responses without losing track, even when it pauses before finishing. If you were watching, you'd see it respond in chunks and continue smoothly from where it left off instead of stopping or getting confused. This only affects the internal system that processes your requests, so nothing about your account or access changed.

ai.title: Add Jest testing infrastructure to backend
ai.summary: Introduced Jest, ts-jest, and @types/jest to backend/package.json devDependencies. Added 'test' and 'test:watch' scripts to enable unit testing. This establishes the testing framework for the backend service.

eli5.text: The team gave the backend a built-in way to automatically check itself for mistakes, similar to how spell-check works for a document. When they make future changes to the assistant's behind-the-scenes logic, it can now catch problems before they reach you. This only affects the staff building and updating the assistant, not your experience right now, since it's purely a tool to help them work more carefully.

ai.title: Add Jest config and refactor Claude continuation logic
ai.summary: Introduced `backend/jest.config.js` and updated `backend/tsconfig.json` to enable unit testing. Moved `promptClaudeWithContinuation` from `backend/src/prompts.ts` to `backend/src/claude.ts`, simplifying it by removing tool call handling from the loop. Exported `generateDiffBlocks` for testing and added instruction 7 to diff generation prompts to strip meta-comments.

eli5.text: The team added a testing system behind the scenes so the assistant can now automatically check that its responses stay consistent over time, mainly benefitting developers building on the platform today. They also moved the assistant's continuation logic into its own folder and simplified how it handles follow-up answers, though most readers won't notice this directly. Additionally, the assistant now strips out meta-comments from code changes it generates, but this only affects developers reviewing the diff output.

ai.title: Improve generation continuation and add code review/planning prompts
ai.summary: The generation continuation logic in `backend/src/prompts.ts` was refined to strip the last line of the partial response before resuming, preventing repetition. The system prompt in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` now instructs the model to use `<code_review>` and `<planning>` blocks for complex tasks. `STOP_MARKER` was moved from `common/src/prompts.ts` to `common/src/constants.ts` to better reflect its nature.

eli5.text: When the AI assistant is writing code and gets cut off mid-sentence, it now removes the last incomplete line before continuing, so it doesn't repeat itself. The instructions given to the AI now ask it to write a special <code_review> block to explain complex code and a <planning> block when figuring out a tricky task. You'd notice this if you asked the tool to do something complicated and saw it structure its response with labeled sections for review and planning before giving you the final answer.

ai.title: Update ts-node script and tsconfig include path
ai.summary: The `code` script in `package.json` now points to `src/index.ts` instead of `index.ts`. The `include` array in `tsconfig.json` was updated to remove the root `index.ts` file, retaining only `src/**/*`. This aligns the build and execution entry points with the current source directory structure.

eli5.text: The assistant's underlying code now loads from a single consolidated folder, so the place it reads its startup instructions from was adjusted to keep everything in the right spot. You wouldn't see a difference in how it behaves, but the system that builds and runs the assistant now points to the same main file in both the build step and the run command, preventing it from accidentally loading an old or duplicate starting point.

ai.title: Rename scoped @manicode/common package to plain common
ai.summary: Renamed package `@manicode/common` to `common` in `package.json` files. Updated import paths across `backend`, `src`, and `common` to use the shorter name (e.g., `common/util/file` instead of `@manicode/common/src/util/file`). Adjusted `tsconfig.json` path mappings and `jest.config.js` module resolution to support the new alias. This simplifies internal dependency references and reduces import verbosity.

eli5.text: Today, when the assistant looks up shared pieces of its memory (like rules, past messages, or project notes), it reaches for them under a shorter name. The change renames how that shared memory package is labeled across the project: instead of a long, scoped tag, it now uses a plain, simple word. You won't see this yourself, as a user of the assistant, but it makes the behind-the-scenes wiring cleaner and the code easier for the team to maintain. If you looked at the source files, you'd notice import statements using a simpler path instead of a long, prefixed one.

ai.title: Add Jest setup file for backend environment variables
ai.summary: New `backend/jest.setup.js` loads `.env` via `dotenv` for Jest runs. `backend/jest.config.js` registers it in `setupFilesAfterEnv`. Ensures backend tests have access to environment variables.

eli5.text: When the software runs its automated backend tests, it now automatically reads the same configuration settings (like API keys and database paths) that it uses in normal operation, instead of starting up empty. Previously those tests ran without any environment settings loaded, so anything depending on them would fail or behave differently than expected; now they load that configuration at the very start of the test run. If you looked, you'd notice the test runner quietly logs a message about loading environment variables before any tests begin, and backend tests that rely on those settings now work consistently instead of being skipped or erroring out.

ai.title: Remove common barrel export
ai.summary: Deleted `common/src/index.ts` barrel file. `src/claude.ts` and `src/project-files.ts` now import `removeUndefinedProps` and `filterObject` directly from `common/util/object`. Removed `console.log` for file updates in `applyChanges`. Forces explicit module paths for shared utilities.

eli5.text: You won't see a visible change in how the app works, but behind the scenes the team removed an old collection of shared tools and now each part of the app grabs just the specific helper it needs directly. This makes the code easier to follow and keeps unused bits from sneaking in. While doing this, they also stopped printing a small message in the logs whenever a file was updated or created. The app behaves the same way today; these are internal cleanups to keep the project tidy.

ai.title: Simplify CLI console output and file exclusion logic
ai.summary: Reduced verbose console messages in `src/index.ts`, replacing multi-line file change reports with single-line status updates. Exit handling simplified by removing explicit keyword checks for 'exit'/'quit' in favor of standard readline closure. `src/project-files.ts` refactored to pass `excludedDirs` directly to `loadAllProjectFiles`, eliminating post-filtering of `node_modules`, `dist`, and `.git`.

eli5.text: The assistant no longer prints a long list of every file it changes to your screen; instead, it shows a short one-line message for each file it creates or updates. It also stops searching inside folders like node_modules, dist, and.git when figuring out which project files to pay attention to, so it ignores those internal folders from the start rather than filtering them out afterward. If you use the assistant from the command line, you will see less scrolling text and slightly faster, cleaner responses.

ai.title: Add instant Escape interrupt and partial response handling
ai.summary: Implemented immediate response termination on ESC key press, clearing terminal line and resetting state to prompt user. Added `responseBuffer` to capture streamed content, saving partial responses with `[RESPONSE_STOPPED_BY_USER]` marker if interrupted. Refactored input loop into `promptUser` function for recursive handling after stop. Updated `musings.knowledge.md` with note on indicating diff generation status.

eli5.text: When the assistant is generating a reply, pressing the Escape key now immediately stops the response mid-stream instead of waiting for it to finish. You will see the current line cleared and a note that the response was stopped by you, then the assistant asks for your next input. The change affects anyone using the interactive terminal version of the tool and is live now, since it modifies how the main input loop behaves. A related note in the internal docs also asks the system to tell the client when it is still planning file changes, so interruptions like this can be handled more cleanly in the future.

ai.title: Clarify codereview and planning trigger conditions
ai.summary: System prompt instructions for <code_review> and <planning> blocks tightened. <code_review> now mandates post-file-read context; <planning> requires understanding both request and code. Scope: backend/src/system-prompt.ts, backend/src/claude.ts (added continuation debug logs), musings.knowledge.md (tracked issues).

eli5.text: The assistant's built-in helper that explains code to itself got stricter rules: it now must actually read a file before summarizing it, and it must understand both your question and the existing code before drawing up a plan. Anyone working with or watching the assistant will notice it pauses a bit longer to review what it's about to change, rather than jumping straight to an answer. A small trail of extra debug notes was also left in the system logs so developers can see when the assistant is continuing a multi-step response. The change is live today.

ai.title: Replace readline with raw stdin for arrow key history
ai.summary: src/index.ts drops `readline.createInterface` for manual `process.stdin` raw mode handling. Implements `history` array and `historyIndex` to support Up/Down arrow cycling through previous inputs. `promptUser` now writes `> ` directly via `process.stdout.write`.

eli5.text: When you open the assistant and are waiting for a prompt, you can now press the up and down arrow keys to cycle through commands or messages you typed earlier in this session, instead of retyping them. Rather than relying on a built-in input handler, the program now reads each key you press directly from your keyboard, which is what makes remembering and recalling past entries possible.
